# AIPerf — Python orchestrator + native runner session-bootstrap index

Single-page topology of the important source + design files, with a one-line
purpose for each, so an agent knows which file to open for a given question.

## ✅ Canonical / ⛔️ deprecated

- **CANONICAL PRODUCT PATH:** the human-facing `aiperf` command IS the ONE native
  binary (crate `aiperf-cli`) — it owns `profile`/`config` natively
  (byte-exact Config v2), projects one protocol-v2 request, and drives execution
  by re-execing ITSELF (`aiperf --execute`), delegating only peripheral subcommands
  (`plot`/`service`/`plugins`) to Python (embedded CPython, or `python -m aiperf`
  in the lean build).
  Config v2's schema, planning, outer loops, and presentation stay Python-defined.
  The one `aiperf` binary is BOTH the entry point AND the execution engine — the sole
  executable that dispatches load and owns exactly one benchmark hot path (no separate
  runner binary). The runtime library it links is crate `aiperf-runtime` (`rust/runtime`).
  The standalone `aiperf-mock-server`
  developer/test target is an ordinary online inference server, not an
  orchestrated backend process. `rust/runtime` is a runtime library and
  intentionally has no binary target (the native binary is the `aiperf-cli` crate).
- **DEPRECATED:** the `aiperf-rs` and `~/projects/aiperf-rust` trees (mechanical
  1:1 ports that reproduce the Python multiprocess/ZMQ complexity this design
  deletes). Do not build on them.
- **OWNERSHIP:** Rust execution truth is `rust/`; canonical Python frontend
  truth includes `src/aiperf/config`, `src/aiperf/orchestrator`, and
  `src/aiperf/cli_runner`. The old controller/service/ZMQ implementation under
  `src/` remains legacy and is not an alternate hot path.
- **Agent instructions:** `CLAUDE.md` = `AGENTS.md` = `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
  = `.cursor/rules/python.mdc` (byte-identical body; keep in sync via
  `python tools/check_agent_files_sync.py`).

## The architecture in one breath

The native `aiperf` binary projects one side-effect-free authored request and
re-execs itself (`aiperf --execute`) to run it; the Python frontend is pure
Python (legacy service mesh only) and does not bridge to Rust — there is no
Python request projection, protocol-v1 resolver, conversion, or fallback. The execution engine exact-image-preflights the requested transport and workload
and direct-loads their registered adapters (any workload runs over any transport;
there is no pair map or compatibility gate). It drives **ONLINE-real** over
native HTTP or gRPC (including KServe OIP and NVIDIA Riva ASR/TTS/NLP) and
**ONLINE-mock** over HTTP through one `{transport,
clock}` seam. The base image registers HTTP scheduled/graph/static-accuracy/
agentic and native gRPC scheduled execution. **OFFLINE-mock** is product-
reachable through the same Python Config-v2 path when the runner is built with
the non-default `dynosim` feature; that image adds `dynosim_offline` and
`dynosim_online` scheduled and graph execution. Unregistered transports or
workloads fail closed.
The open `vllm_generate` endpoint is token-native end to end: its descriptor
requires validated raw IDs, `aiperf-dataset` stores them as content-addressed
handles and generates synthetic IDs without decoding text, online HTTP maps
them to `/inference/v1/generate`, and Dynamo-offline resolves the same handle
without constructing a request body or invoking an encoder. Returned ID arrays
remain non-text response data and drive exact token/usage observations.
Direct Graph-IR currently lacks that linear-dataset handle and fails preparation
for endpoints with the requirement.
Generated image/video delivery can be externalized through one run-owned native
content server. Python projects `AIPERF_CONTENT_SERVER_*` into a strict v2
sidecar input; `aiperf-dataset` injects inline or file/URL publication; the
runner binds, tracks, and drains `aiperf-content-server`. Audio remains inline.
Scheduled/graph/static-accuracy online HTTP execute the sidecar;
agentic/evaluation, native gRPC, and offline pairs reject it.
Time lives behind `Clock` (`RealClock` vs
integer-ns DES `SimClock`); dispatch lives behind `RequestSink<R>` +
`RequestObserver` into a `TraceCollector`; token callbacks can carry
`ObservedTokenKind::{Output,Reasoning}` and fall back to unclassified `on_token`,
while terminal `ObservedUsage` carries endpoint counts as optional fields.
`is_virtual()` picks the `drive_real`
(reactor) vs `drive_sim` (idle-pump) driver over the *same* executor.
`RequestObserver` is intentionally local-loop (`!Send`/`!Sync`) so returned-event
fan-out and collection use `Rc`/`RefCell` without per-token locks. Thread-per-core,
`Rc`/`RefCell`, `!Send`, `spawn_local` on the hot path.

Offline/online Dynamo replay is authored through `aiperf profile` as Config-v2
transports (`transport.type: dynosim_offline` / `dynosim_online`), not a
separate command. The typed `DynosimTransportConfig`
(`src/aiperf/config/dynosim.py`) mirrors the runner's `DynosimTransportSpec` and
projects verbatim into the protocol-v2 request; trace and concurrency reuse the
shared `dataset`/`phases` surface. There is no `replay_mode` field. The live
Dynamo mocker server and the replay-optimize sweep remain native
`python -m dynamo.*` tools.

Native recorded-graph compilation is built for recursive WEKA objects and
`dynamo.request.trace.v1` JSONL/gzip/segmented captures. Both enter one
runner-owned graph-input resolver, share one LCP-trie lowerer, and produce dense
segments plus Graph-IR without a Python trace data plane. Content synthesis uses
the existing `aiperf-rng` BLAKE3/PCG64 stream only; there is no Python SHA/MT
duplicate. Equivalent logical WEKA and Dynamo inputs produce byte-identical
native segments and HTTP bodies under that canonical stream.

## Crate topology (`rust/`)

| Crate | Read for | Entry files |
|---|---|---|
| `loadgen-core` (`rust/loadgen-core`) | the transport-neutral dispatch/measure seam + report: `Dispatchable`, `RequestSink<R>`, local-loop `RequestObserver` (no `Send`/`Sync`; optional token classification; terminal usage with optional fields), `TraceCollector`, `TraceSimulationReport` | `src/sink.rs`, `src/collector.rs`, `src/observer.rs` |
| `aiperf-runtime` (`rust/runtime`, library-only — no binary) | the whole native runtime the `aiperf` binary links: the `{clock}` seam, prepared HTTP/gRPC sinks, online paced/scheduled/adaptive/static-accuracy paths, the provider-neutral evaluation workload/host registry/arbiter/ledger/report join, legacy stateful agentic seams, datasets/segments, the metrics engine, the Graph-IR runtime, telemetry side-channels, and the native export plane. Owns the single `AIPerfRegistry`/`AIPerfExtension` composition seam (`extensions/`) and, behind the `engine` Cargo feature that ONLY `aiperf-cli` enables, hosts the relocated v2 layer `aiperf_runtime::engine` (protocol/registry, execution factories and drivers, coordinator, `Application`, cellular controller/cell, control-plane HTTP, GPU/network/server side-channels). Sixteen former `aiperf-*` library crates are now its `aiperf_runtime::<module>` modules | `src/lib.rs`, `extensions/`, `engine/`, `transport/http/sink.rs`, `transport/grpc/sink.rs`, `run.rs`, `scheduled.rs`, `phase_runtime.rs`, `evaluation.rs`, `metrics.rs`, `report.rs`, and the module dirs (`clock/`, `rng/`, `timing/`, `dataset/`, `endpoints/`, `graph/`, `metrics_core/`, `adaptive_core/`, `accuracy_core/`, `transport/` (`core`/`http`/`grpc`), `content_server/`, `gpu_telemetry/`, `server_metrics/`, `network_latency/`) |
| `aiperf-mock-server` | standalone online test/benchmark inference target: OpenAI chat/completions/embeddings, TGI, rerank, image, multimodal, and RAG routes; real SSE; analytic/batch-scheduler latency; deterministic token generation; prefix-cache policy; Prometheus dialects; and synthetic DCGM telemetry. Optional `--grpc-port` adds a KServe OIP v2 `GRPCInferenceService` (`ModelInfer`/`ModelStreamInfer`/`ModelReady`/`ServerLive`/`ServerReady`) over h2c, reusing the same generation seam and the `aiperf_runtime::transport::grpc::proto` prost messages (no build-time protoc); HTTP-only under `--processes N`. An optional `--accuracy-dataset <path>` loads a JSONL `{prompt, ground_truth}` dataset and returns the grader-formatted correct answer for a seeded fraction of matched prompts (`--accuracy-correct-rate`/`--accuracy-format`), with chain-of-thought (`--accuracy-cot-rate`) and parser-choke adversarial shapes (`--accuracy-adversarial-rate`: reasoning-only #1136, `object:null` stream frame #1010, whitespace/case/boxed/conflicting/unicode); ground truth is loaded mock-side and keyed on the prompt (`--accuracy-match` exact/substring/`_ci` modes + per-row `match_key`; never sent over the wire). A live `GET /accuracy` endpoint plus `aiperf_mock_accuracy_*` Prometheus metrics report the run's actual served correct/matched tally. Also closes runner-to-mock e2e gaps (each raw-export tested): configurable error injection (status menu/Retry-After/mid-stream SSE), extended `--usage-*` accounting, `tool_calls` emission, `/v1/responses` + `/inference/v1/generate` + `/openai/v1/*` + KServe HTTP v2/v1 routes, gRPC KServe rankings/images/VLM tensors (`--grpc-behavior`), Riva ASR/TTS/NLP gRPC, `--uds` Unix-socket listener, and TLS/`grpcs` (`--tls-*`). Exports both a test router and a tuned Hyper server binary; not a runner dependency | `src/app.rs`, `src/grpc.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `src/handlers.rs`, `src/tokens.rs`, `src/latency.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`, `src/prefix_cache.rs`, `src/metrics.rs`, `src/prom.rs`, `src/dcgm.rs`, `src/accuracy.rs`, `src/grpc_riva.rs`, `src/tls.rs`, `src/main.rs` |
| `aiperf-cli` (binary `aiperf`) | native Rust entry point (crate `aiperf-cli`, lib + bin) that owns `aiperf profile` (single run **and** grid/zip sweeps) and `aiperf config init/validate/expand` — no Python on the profile/config path: clap flags + serde Config v2 projected onto the `protocol_v2` schema, re-execing ITSELF (`aiperf --execute`) once per sweep cell, aggregated into `sweep_aggregate/`, with the console summary echoed to the terminal. It is BOTH the entry point AND the execution engine (no separate runner binary; capabilities is the in-process `execute_mode::capabilities_catalog` fn). Comma-list flags expand natively (`sweep/`, alpha-sorted axes, byte-exact per-cell requests, artifact-dir 5-row table, `base+idx` seeds); `--num-profile-runs N` adds N trials per variation (byte-exact dirs/seeds). Single-trial sweeps write a byte-exact `sweep_aggregate/profile_export_aiperf_sweep.{json,csv}`; multi-trial confidence aggregate deferred (scipy t-dist). `config init` scaffolds 28 embedded templates; `config validate` applies `${ENV}` + Jinja2 expansion (`expand.rs`), inline dataset `records:`, and the distribution discriminator; a config `sweep:` block (grid/zip dotted-path axes, `sweep/yaml_sweep.rs`) expands natively and previews via `config expand`. Native profile/config byte-exact vs Python for every modeled flag (all GenAI-Perf aliases; zero pure-alias gaps; scenario/trajectory/unsafe/agentic + always-emitted accuracy/endpoint_profiles/failure_policy land natively). NEVER shells to the Python profile command — request projection is native for every modeled flag (media/rankings/synthesis/scenario/dataset-filter/search all golden-verified); accuracy execution uses the pinned Python evaluators (sanctioned in-process/subprocess path), never the Python profile command. The adaptive **SLA-search** subsystem is built: all four `max-concurrency-under-sla --search-style` styles run natively as dynamic ask-tell loops (one `aiperf --execute` child per probe, SLA metric read from `native-v2.json`) — `monotonic` pure-Rust; default `smooth_isotonic` (scipy PAVA+PCHIP), `bo` (BoTorchSampler+qLogNEI), `optuna` (TPE/GP) behind the opt-in `search-pyo3` feature (embeds CPython; default binary stays Python-free). Peripheral subcommands native pure-Rust (no pyo3): `analyze-trace`, `validate mooncake-trace`, `speed-bench-report`, `chat` (hyper streaming client + stats), and `synthesize agentic-code` (seeded dataset generator on the byte-exact numpy `Generator` port `aiperf_runtime::rng::numpy_generator`) — all byte-exact vs Python. Heavier subcommands (plot=matplotlib, service=legacy mesh, plugins) run in-process via embedded CPython in the `pyo3-embed`/`search-pyo3` build (zero subprocess), else a `python -m aiperf` subprocess in the lean build. Parity: `tools/parity/` (`dump_golden.py` single-run, `dump_sweep.py`, `dump_sweep_aggregate.py`, and dynamic-search `dump_monotonic.py`/`dump_isotonic.py`/`dump_bayes.py` byte-exact on pure-Rust+seeded-TPE) | `rust/cli/src/{main.rs,lib.rs,dispatch.rs,delegate.rs,profile.rs,flags.rs,load.rs,yaml.rs,execute.rs,exec_bin.rs,execute_mode.rs,render.rs,search.rs,isotonic.rs,bayes.rs,pyfit.rs,pyopt.rs}`, `rust/cli/src/{sweep,config}/`, `mimalloc_options.c`/`build.rs` |
| `pyext` (module `aiperf._native`, `rust/pyext`) | packaging-only pyo3 `cdylib`: maturin's compiled target (`aiperf._native`) alongside the packaged `src/aiperf` frontend (`python-source = "src"`). It does NOT build the unified `aiperf` binary — `tools/wheel_repack.py` (run by `make wheel`) repacks that binary directly into the wheel's scripts directory as `aiperf-<ver>.data/scripts/aiperf`, so the installed `aiperf` command IS the native binary (there is no `[project.scripts] aiperf` console-script entry; the pure-Python app is reachable as `aiperf-python` = `aiperf.entrypoint:main`, and `python -m aiperf`). No internal deps; carries only `aiperf --version` build metadata; never imported at runtime | `rust/pyext/Cargo.toml`, `rust/pyext/src/lib.rs` |
| `aiperf-e2e-tests` (`rust/e2e`) | the end-to-end harness: drives the Python `aiperf profile` entry point against `aiperf-mock-server` and verifies the raw per-record JSONL (`profile_export_raw.jsonl`) for timing + data. Builds without the `engine` layer | `rust/e2e/tests/`, `rust/e2e/tests/common/` |

The six workspace crates are `loadgen-core`, `aiperf-runtime`, `aiperf-cli`, `aiperf-mock-server`, `pyext`, and `aiperf-e2e-tests`. Sixteen former `aiperf-*` library crates are now modules of `aiperf-runtime` (`aiperf_runtime::<m>`): `clock`, `rng`, `metrics_core`, `timing`, `adaptive_core`, `accuracy_core`, `endpoints`, `dataset`, `content_server`, `extensions`, `transport` (with `transport::core` vocabulary + `transport::http`/`transport::grpc` wire impls), `graph`, `gpu_telemetry`, `server_metrics`, `network_latency`, plus the feature-gated `engine`. Per-module purpose + key files: [`docs/module-organization.md`](docs/module-organization.md).

Deps: `aiperf-cli` → {`aiperf-runtime` (with the `engine` feature), `loadgen-core`} and re-execs ITSELF (`aiperf --execute`) at runtime (a launched process, not a second binary); `aiperf-runtime` → {`loadgen-core`} plus optional `dynamo-mocker` only under `dynosim`; `aiperf-mock-server` → {`aiperf-runtime`}; `pyext` → {`pyo3`} only (no internal deps, nothing depends on it). Within `aiperf-runtime` the modules compose through `crate::<module>::` imports: `metrics_core` stays IO-free and runtime-neutral, and the `gpu_telemetry`/`server_metrics`/`network_latency` telemetry producers feed the shared side-channel accumulator seam without core metrics ever depending back on a producer. `aiperf-cli` and `aiperf-mock-server` do not depend on each other; real-network tests spawn the mock binary as an ordinary target.

## Run AIPerf

```bash
# Generate, validate, and run through the only user-facing entry point.
aiperf config init --template minimal --output benchmark.yaml
aiperf config validate benchmark.yaml
aiperf profile --config benchmark.yaml

# Externalize generated images/videos through the run-owned native server.
mkdir -p /tmp/aiperf-content
AIPERF_CONTENT_SERVER_ENABLED=true \
  AIPERF_CONTENT_SERVER_CONTENT_DIR=/tmp/aiperf-content \
  aiperf profile --config benchmark.yaml

# Cellular (multi-process) mode: `--cells N` (or `runtime.cells: N`) makes the launched
# aiperf a controller that spawns N `aiperf --cell` children over a
# (cell_id, cell_count) budget partition and merges their records into one report.
# `--cells 1` (default) is the unchanged single-process path. Supported for synthetic,
# single-turn runs over the http OR grpc transport with request-bounded phases (gRPC runs
# the SAME cell executor as http — the cell issuer + records shipper live above the
# transport); a run seed and single URL are NOT required (seedless auto-derives a shared
# seed, multi-URL round-robins cell-locally, ramps/rate/cancellation aggregate-equivalent,
# warned). Graph programs (dag_jsonl/weka_trace/dynamo_trace) also partition across cells
# (trace-level, concatenation-merged; a --sketch-metrics graph cell ships a folded sketch
# store, merged like exact-fold). Fails closed on the dynosim offline/online transport +
# scheduled duration/adaptive. E2e: test_cellular.rs + test_grpc_cellular.rs (scheduled) +
# test_graph_cellular.rs (incl. sketch store-ship).
aiperf profile --config benchmark.yaml --cells 4

# Developer-only runner protocol inventory; normal runs are launched by Python.
# capabilities is in-process now (aiperf_cli::execute_mode::capabilities_catalog); no --capabilities argv mode
```

`cargo run -p aiperf-runtime` is intentionally invalid: the `aiperf-runtime` Rust
package has no binary. Config-v2 YAML expresses endpoints, datasets, phases, ramps,
cancellation, adaptive policy, static/stateful accuracy, provider-neutral
evaluation, telemetry, artifacts, and open
transport/workload selections. Python expands outer loops; execution retains the
side-effect-free authored-v2 shape through validation and execution. It
requires the selected runner image to advertise the exact pair and never
resolves or converts the run to protocol v1. Explicit open workloads delegate
phase-stop semantics to their registered Rust factory; implicit built-in
workloads retain Python's generic stop validation. `dag_jsonl`, `weka_trace`,
and `dynamo_trace` enter the runner-owned Graph-IR input adapter once and invoke
exactly one selected compiler, lowering directly to graph plans plus one frozen
segment store without a second registry or linear dataset intermediate.
Recorded formats accept `synthesis.max_osl`, `max_context_length`,
`idle_gap_cap_seconds`, `corpus`, and `allow_dataset_wrap` where applicable;
Python forwards those authored values without parsing trace payloads. Native gRPC requires
`transport.type: grpc` with `grpc://` or `grpcs://` URLs, behind the default-on
`grpc` Cargo feature (a lean HTTP-only build drops it and `tonic`); offline/wall-clock
in-process Dynamo replay requires `transport.type: dynosim_offline` or
`transport.type: dynosim_online` and a feature-bearing runner. Each native
transport (`http`/`grpc`/`dry_run`) is resolved from the transport registry
through its `NativeTransportExecution` binding, so the scheduled/graph workloads
never branch on a transport enum. There is ONE thread-per-core execution model:
`workers==1` runs a single co-located `WorkerSink` on the coordinator reactor
(`turn_execution::build_native`), and `workers>1` tiles that same sink across `W`
self-contained sub-cells (`sharded_scheduled::run_sharded_scheduled`) — no
cross-thread per-request hop (the former `ThreadPerCoreExecutor` was deleted).
Every workload shape shards (rate/concurrency by budget, user_centric/
fixed_schedule per conversation, static-accuracy by per-shard capture graded once
at finalize; `shardable` is just `workers > 1`). A transport contributes only a
`WorkerSink` via an `ExecutionSinkBuilder`, never its own worker loop/measurement
(`transport::reduce`/`transport::measure` are shared) — gRPC has no parallel
execution path. Adding a transport is writing a sink builder and registering a
factory; gating one out is not registering it.

Provider-neutral evaluation additionally requires the selected runner
deployment's wheel-`RECORD`-verified companion roots or generated adjacent
root-registry sidecar. Missing or drifted roots make the evaluator distributions
unavailable and omit `http + evaluation`; Python does not substitute an
ambient provider environment or a legacy workload.

Content-server validation is side-effect-free. Image/video URL publication
requires both `AIPERF_CONTENT_SERVER_ENABLED=true` and a non-empty existing
`AIPERF_CONTENT_SERVER_CONTENT_DIR`; enabled with an empty directory starts a
temporary server but keeps media inline. See `docs/tutorials/content-server.md`.

`AIPERF_RNG_BACKEND=rust_parity` (default `legacy`) swaps the seeded random
substrate from Python's Mersenne Twister + NumPy (SHA-256 derivation) to a
pure-Python byte-exact port of the Rust `aiperf_runtime::rng` `Pcg64` + BLAKE3 substrate
(`src/aiperf/common/rng_parity/`), so seeded Python and Rust produce identical
streams in tests. `Environment.RNG.BACKEND` in `src/aiperf/common/environment.py`;
parity is proved against committed Rust golden vectors
(`rust/runtime/examples/rng_parity_vectors.rs` ->
`rust/runtime/tests/data/rng_parity_vectors.json`).

The online concurrency and request-rate issuers own all applicable live ramp
actuators. User-centric owns only its optional session-concurrency pool, while
fixed schedule owns none; unsupported ramps fail validation rather than becoming
inert. Scheduled strategies support per-turn cancellation and turn-zero sticky
endpoint routing.

## Canonical static accuracy

Static accuracy is configured through Config v2 and launched by
`aiperf profile --config ...`. Python selects the pinned evaluator environment;
the runner supervises it while retaining all inference traffic and timing.

Rust sends every LLM request and parses every response through its normal
transport. The Python/Lighteval child prepares opaque problems and batch-grades
terminal response text; it never contacts the inference server, and ground
truth/private tests never cross the JSONL protocol. The evaluator protocol rejects
unknown static-response fields and restricts static prompts to `{role, content}`; stateful
agent/tool messages retain role-specific fields losslessly. The worker redirects
ambient fd 1 output to stderr and native v2 records its source/lock identity.

## Stateful agentic accuracy

The Harbor, AgentLab/BrowserGym, and MCPMark providers and Rust
`AgenticWorkload` are product-reachable through the registered
`http + agentic` protocol-v2 pair. Real subprocess proofs cover the
supervised evaluator, authenticated callback gateway, ordinary Rust HTTP/SSE
dispatch, and scored native-v2 report. Do not add a second CLI or move model
traffic into Python.

Harbor owns task packages, Terminus-2, environments, trajectories, terminal
execution, and verifier rewards. Primary calls use its queue callback. Packaged
LLM-backed environments/verifiers receive an authenticated callback address;
Rust's ingress converts those calls to the same scheduled workload and never
forwards directly. Rust issues every turn through the generic online
scheduled/transport runner. Native v2 records exact worker/lock/container,
harness source/version, dataset revision, agent, environment, verifier, authored
configuration, canonical rewards, episode records, and artifacts. Infrastructure
and cancellation records are never converted into zero/incorrect scores.
Harbor's canonical source forms are accepted unchanged: Hub
`org/name@ref`, legacy `name@version` (for example `bfcl@1.0`), and an existing
local task-directory path. Hub tags are reported as resolved content hashes;
legacy versions are frozen before Harbor enumerates their tasks.

The removed native-CLI route remains deleted; product proofs launch only the
strict runner through Python's Config-v2 path.

AgentLab 0.4.2 plus BrowserGym 0.14.3 is the canonical browser provider. It
directly runs `DEFAULT_BENCHMARKS`, `GenericAgent`, and `ExpArgs`; its sync model
callback emits JSONL and only a Rust terminal result can resume the browser
loop. BrowserGym owns prompts, actions, Playwright transitions, traces, and
rewards. Browser tasks use dependency-safe sequential admission. The separately
hashed worker lock is required because AgentLab's OpenAI <2 constraint conflicts
with Harbor's LiteLLM/OpenAI 2.x constraint.

MCPMark commit `cd45b7f57923b9b3985467f5139927575f83141c` is a third
independently hash-locked provider. MCPMark owns the registry, task instructions,
100-turn loop, MCP servers, state managers, task-local `verify.py`, artifacts,
and cleanup. AIPerf replaces only `litellm.acompletion` with its JSONL broker;
Python never receives a model-server URL. Native v2 records MCPMark's exact
source/lock, canonical agent controls, selected server artifact, task digest,
and concrete local-environment digest.

## Run the scheduled workloads

Request-rate, concurrency, user-centric, and fixed-schedule strategies are
Config-v2 phase variants executed by the runner. See
`src/aiperf/config/templates/{latency_test,multi_turn_conversation,fixed_schedule}.yaml`
for runnable examples.

Fixed-trace zero/window policy is expressed in the Config-v2 fixed-schedule
phase. Rust records scheduled, issued, dispatch, first-token, TTFT, terminal,
and aggregate lateness facts in the native result/artifacts selected by Python.

## AIPerf offline engine

The workspace root expects `../../../dynamo-aiperf-native`. Library developers
can compile the adapter; `dynamo-full` enables every optional mocker family:

```bash
cargo build -p aiperf-runtime --features dynosim
cargo test -p aiperf-runtime --features dynosim --lib
cargo build -p aiperf-cli --features dynosim
```

There is no native `--offline` CLI. An `aiperf` binary built with `dynosim`
registers `dynosim + scheduled` and `dynosim + graph`; Python
authors the same Config-v2 request and exact-image preflight rejects a base
runner that does not advertise those pairs.

Single, aggregate, and disaggregate topologies, both routers, all five trace
formats, cancellation, ramps, adaptive controls, SLA goodput, and raw/timed
artifacts run on one `SimClock` with no inference server. Before any offline API
returns, the complete common flat reports must serialize to identical compact
JSON bytes: 74 base fields, plus three goodput fields when configured. Multi-
phase runs retain the independent compatibility observer; single-phase product
runs avoid that duplicate row store and reconstruct the byte-equal compatibility
report from Dynamo after drain while native metrics remain callback-driven.
Requested KV offload fails closed on initialization error. Canonical accuracy
alone remains online because the timing engine does not generate semantic answer
text.

## Run offline/online Dynamo replay through `aiperf profile`

```bash
# transport.type: dynosim_offline|dynosim_online; offline is byte-exact with native replay.
aiperf profile --config dynosim_offline_replay.yaml
```

This requires an `aiperf` binary (crate `aiperf-cli`) built with the `dynosim` Cargo feature (and the
sibling `dynamo-aiperf-native` checkout). There is no `replay_mode` field; the
transport ID selects virtual or wall-clock replay. The live Dynamo mocker server and the
replay-optimize sweep remain native tools: `python -m dynamo.mocker` and Dynamo's
profiler.

## "Which file answers…" quick map

- **How is virtual time deterministic?** `rust/runtime/src/clock/sim_clock.rs`
  (min-heap, `(at_ns, seq_no)`, `advance_to`) + `rust/runtime/src/graph/runtime.rs`
  (`drive_sim` and `drive_sim_with_source` idle-pumps).
- **How is a request dispatched + measured?** `rust/loadgen-core/src/sink.rs` (traits)
  → `rust/runtime/src/http.rs` (`TransportSink`) →
  `rust/loadgen-core/src/observer.rs` (`CollectorObserver`).
- **Where is evaluator ownership split?** Provider-neutral control/isolation lives
  in `rust/runtime/src/accuracy_core/{provider,provider_protocol,supervisor,isolation,artifacts}.rs`;
  Rust-owned host effects, admission, ledger, proxy, sealing, and report join live
  in `rust/runtime/src/evaluation{.rs,/}`; the provider-neutral host seam lives under
  `src/aiperf/accuracy/evaluation/`. Legacy static/stateful ownership remains in
  `rust/runtime/src/accuracy_core/{protocol,worker}.rs`,
  `src/aiperf/accuracy/{worker,agentic,model_broker,harbor,harbor_agent,browsergym,mcpmark}.py`,
  `rust/runtime/src/{accuracy,agentic,agentic_gateway}.rs`, and
  `rust/runtime/src/engine/agentic_execution.rs` until its exact deletion gates pass.
- **Where do native TTFT/ITL/e2e/throughput/goodput and sweeps come from?**
  `rust/runtime/src/metrics.rs` (runtime join) → `rust/runtime/src/metrics_core/{store,accumulator,sweepline}.rs`.
  `rust/runtime/src/http.rs` also translates the real transport trace into HTTP metric facts;
  `rust/loadgen-core/src/collector.rs` remains the compact compatibility summary.
- **Where are streamed chunks and usage parsed?** `rust/runtime/src/endpoints/chat_chunk.rs`
  (`ChatChunk`, `Usage`) + `rust/loadgen-core/src/observer.rs` (delta-token recorder).
  `rust/runtime/src/http.rs` emits terminal usage and `metrics_core` reconciles
  collector-wide completion counts while retaining observed chunk timings.
- **How does the online loop work?** `rust/runtime/src/run.rs` (Clock-paced arrival
  generator, dynamic session/prefill `SlotPool`s, `StopChecker`, adaptive task).
- **How do user-centric and fixed-schedule runs work?**
  `rust/runtime/src/{scheduled,scheduler,user_centric,fixed_schedule,multiturn}.rs`;
  exact virtual-time coverage is in `rust/runtime/tests/scheduled_sim.rs`, and real HTTP
  library timing coverage is in `rust/runtime/tests/scheduled_real_mock.rs`.
- **How does adaptive scale work?** `rust/runtime/src/adaptive_core/{window,sla,step,controller,runtime}.rs`
  (pure control) → `rust/runtime/src/adaptive.rs` (live-actuator assembly) →
  `rust/runtime/src/run.rs` (backend-neutral online/offline issuer integration).
- **Where do ramps, request cancellation, and sticky endpoint selection live?**
  `rust/runtime/src/timing/{ramping,cancellation,url_selection}.rs` (policy traits) →
  `rust/runtime/src/{ancillary,run,scheduled,http}.rs` (issuer/session wiring) →
  `rust/runtime/src/transport/http/{client,transport}/` (send-complete abort).
- **How does authored DAG input reach graph mode directly?**
  `rust/runtime/src/graph/input.rs` (adapter registry + complete-source parse) →
  `lowering.rs` (`GraphTracePlan` + frozen `SegmentStore`, no linear dataset) →
  `workload.rs` / `placement.rs` → `rust/runtime/src/engine/graph_phase_runtime.rs`
  (one lifecycle/policy driver) → `graph_execution.rs` or `offline_execution.rs`
  (injected backend adapter).
  The throughput harness remains `rust/runtime/src/graph/transport_bench.rs`
  (thread-per-core lanes, transport::http, UDS).
- **How are prompts built without re-serializing?** `rust/runtime/src/dataset/segment.rs`
  (blake3 prefix-dependent dense handles) + `materialize.rs` (wire splice).
- **How are generated media files served?**
  `src/aiperf/{common/environment.py,orchestrator/rust_wire.py}` (public settings
  and strict projection) → `rust/runtime/src/dataset/generator/` (publication seam) →
  `rust/runtime/src/content_server/{publisher,server,tracker}.rs` (file URLs, serving,
  tracking) → `rust/runtime/src/engine/{sidecar_input,online_execution,execute}.rs`
  (strict input, pair preparation, run lifecycle).
- **Where is native-v2 JSON built/written?** `rust/runtime/src/metrics_core/report.rs` →
  `rust/runtime/src/report.rs`; strict run selection/composition is in
  `rust/runtime/src/engine/{protocol_v2,registry,execute}.rs`.

## Design specs (`specs/` — intent, not code)

Full index + status (decided / sketch / superseded): [`specs/README.md`](specs/README.md).

- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-port-exact-vs-redo-ledger.md` — **read first**:
  scope rulings + the credit-policy trap + the three-modes framing. Addendum:
  online/offline parity is shared code path + report schema, not byte-identical values.
- `specs/2026-07-10-shared-rust-architecture-northstar.md` — the target
  abstraction (aspirational vocabulary); its latest addendum replaces the
  native App/CLI layer with Python Config v2 plus the strict runner.
- `specs/2026-07-12-aiperf-rust-crate-naming-layout-design.md` — **decided / not
  implemented; authoritative for crate identity and paths**: AIPerf-owned Cargo
  packages retain `aiperf` / `aiperf-*`, target directories shorten to
  `rust/<capability>`, and `loadgen-core` remains neutral for eventual shared
  use by AIPerf and AI-Dynamo Mocker. The directory migration, independent
  shared-crate versioning, Dynamo consumption, and metadata guard remain unbuilt.
- `specs/2026-07-10-steppable-clock-injected-engine-design.md` — **built and
  runner-reachable behind `dynosim`**: neutral two-source DES pump,
  in-process sink/observer/completion/cancellation seam, all profiles/topologies/
  routers/trace formats, paced/scheduled/graph consumers, SLA/raw/timed artifacts,
  direct raw-token/trace-hash body and encoder bypass, AIC/offload feature
  families, and byte-exact no-server conformance against the sibling Dynamo
  mocker. A feature-bearing runner registers scheduled and graph protocol-v2 pairs.
  Addendum (2026-07-12): the same passive engine also runs under the real wall
  clock (`drive_real_with_source`, selected by `transport.type: dynosim_online`)
  through AIPerf's own flow — apples-to-apples with Dynamo's native
  `simulate_*_live_*` driver (counts exact, latency within 3%, throughput >=
  native); virtual replay uses `transport.type: dynosim_offline`, and there is
  no `replay_mode` config.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-transport-rust-port-design.md` — the Clock-injected
  hyper transport (→ `aiperf-transport-http`); cancellation-after-send is built,
  while complete h2 reuse and aiohttp-style trace-field parity remain narrower
  than the original target.
- `specs/2026-07-12-aiperf-native-grpc-kserve-v2-design.md` — **built +
  addendum**: complete PR-664 KServe endpoint behavior plus the Clock-injected
  Tonic/OIP crate, open gRPC binding registry, typed/raw tensor parity,
  thread-per-core placement, and runner-v2-only HTTP/gRPC scheduled product
  proofs. The 2026-07-12 addendum adds nine NVIDIA Riva ASR/TTS/NLP dialects,
  config-first bidirectional ASR, server-streaming TTS, reference-grounded
  Prost codecs, a real Tonic bidi proof, and a strict Rust runner subprocess.
  KServe V1 Predict remains an endpoint dialect, not runner protocol v1.
- `specs/2026-07-14-mock-server-grpc-kserve-design.md` — **built**: gives
  `aiperf-mock-server` a KServe OIP v2 `GRPCInferenceService` target (dynamo
  parity) so the runner's gRPC KServe client has a mock. Hand-routed tower
  service reusing the shared `aiperf_runtime::transport::grpc::proto` prost messages (no
  build-time protoc); `ModelInfer`/`ModelStreamInfer`/`ModelReady`/`ServerLive`/
  `ServerReady` lower to the mock's chat generation seam; opt-in `--grpc-port`,
  HTTP-only under `--processes N`.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-dataset-segment-seam-design.md` — **built end to
  end + addenda** as `aiperf-dataset`: full loader→compose→dense
  store→sampler→materializer flow shared by the runner, accuracy, and Graph-IR,
  including exact replay, validated raw-token handles, endpoint-required load
  checks, vocabulary-aware no-decode synthesis, decoded/synthetic media,
  context/dispatch fields, and opaque accuracy correlation/task ids; direct `dag_jsonl` bypasses linear
  `Dataset`/`Conversation`/`DagMetadata` composition. Rust no longer stores
  evaluator ground truth.
- `specs/2026-07-12-aiperf-rust-content-server-design.md` — **built**: public
  environment-to-strict-v2 projection, injected inline/file publication,
  stable generated image/video URLs with inline audio, ready-before-use native
  serving, MIME/ranges, canonical traversal/symlink confinement, full streamed-
  body tracking, bounded lifetime-safe telemetry, and run-owned cleanup.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-compile-time-extension-registry-design.md` —
  **built + addenda** statically linked replacement for `plugins.yaml`:
  aggregate transactional registration for dataset formats, samplers, and
  endpoints. `Application` freezes that linked registry with input
  resolvers, pair factories, compatibility authority, and the v2 coordinator;
  capabilities, validation, and execution share the exact object graph.
  Accuracy remains a directly injected evaluator process seam.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-runner-owned-endpoint-registry-design.md` —
  **foundation, v2 validation, and selected prepared execution built; broader convergence pending + addenda; authoritative for endpoint ownership**:
  `aiperf-endpoints` owns open IDs, adapter-local descriptors, deterministic factory/alias
  composition, raw/effective configuration, worker-local prepared bindings/dense keys,
  readiness policy, and compile-once raw/template state; `aiperf-extensions` proves a genuinely
  new dialect. Runner capability and v2 static-validation paths now consume the frozen registry;
  prepared-binding convergence remains. The addendum also
  pins authored preflight, completeness, the strict v2 envelope, and exact image identity;
  mode reachability is intentionally delegated to the next spec.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-runner-only-execution-surface-design.md` — **canonical
  pair matrix built; wire/discovery superseded 2026-07-13**: sole native runner
  and fail-closed reachability remain; request envelope, `supported_pairs`, and
  distribution pinning are superseded by the BenchmarkRun wire + catalog design.
- `specs/2026-07-11-python-orchestrator-rust-single-run-design.md` — **built
  protocol-v2-only product path; wire/projection superseded 2026-07-13**: Python
  CLI/Config ownership and the sole `aiperf --execute` child remain; authored
  `transport`/`workload` projection and “no resolved” rule are superseded by the
  BenchmarkRun wire + catalog design.
- `specs/2026-07-13-benchmarkrun-wire-and-runner-catalog-design.md` — **built
  (performance wire + catalog; dead-mode modules linked but off product wire)**:
  `run` is BenchmarkRun-shaped JSON including `resolved`; the request wire has
  since collapsed to a bare `BenchmarkRun` (operation is the argv mode —
  `--execute` vs `--validate` — not a wire field; the response wire still carries
  `protocol_version`); `--capabilities` emits a
  linked-inventory JSON catalog in `plugins.yaml` category shape; no
  distribution pin / workload / backend dialect; path selection from
  `cfg.transport` + dataset format.
- `specs/2026-07-10-unified-graph-runtime-design.md` — **the realization design**:
  every load mode reduces to one dispatch verb on the clock-scheduled graph
  executor; strategies become `Workload` schedule generators. Supersedes the
  scheduling sketch; addendum maps old RNG wording to BLAKE3 and translates
  north-star seam names to current `RequestSink` / `RequestObserver` symbols.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-request-rate-multiturn-design.md` — **built +
  implementation addendum**: `RequestRateWorkload` is the source-grounded
  single-loop issuer emitting one turn per interval (FIFO continuation-priority,
  NOT conversation arrivals), with session + prefill `SlotPool`s, TTFT/terminal
  release, `StopChecker` bounds, segment-pool materialization, and Clock-deferred
  think time. Synthetic and dataset runner paths share `ScheduledRuntime`; exact
  `SimClock`, real-HTTP, and feature-gated Dynamo tests pin policy and reply splicing.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-user-centric-fixed-schedule-design.md` — **built +
  addendum**: shared Clock-backed `ScheduledRuntime`, conversation/scheduler/source/
  workload traits, user-centric steady-state seeding + churn + continuation pacing,
  and fixed absolute trace replay are wired through Config v2 and the runner. Exact `SimClock`
  and real `aiperf-mock-server` library tests plus runner tests validate ordering,
  drain, timing, TTFT, and reply splicing.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-phase-runner-orchestrator-design.md` — **built +
  implementation addendum**: validated lifecycle/config/progress, direct observers,
  Clock-driven timeout/grace/cancel/drain/force escalation, failure finalization,
  ordered warmup→profiling execution, seamless overlap, and shared-slot debt drain live
  in `aiperf-timing::phase`; `aiperf_runtime::phase_runtime` connects scheduled workloads,
  phase-owned ramps, processors, `SimClock`, and real HTTP. Config v2 and runner
  protocol v2 author ordered warmup/profiling lists. Direct Graph-IR adapts
  `GraphWorkload` through its own execution factory into the same lifecycle,
  including grace/drain/force, seamless handoff, and multiworker control.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-adaptive-scale-design.md` — **built + addendum**:
  `aiperf-adaptive` implements the actuator/evaluator/step/window/controller traits,
  Python-grounded SLA math with authoritative completion-token OSL/ITL reconciliation,
  Clock-paced `ramp_until_fail`, and schema-v2 artifacts;
  online and feature-gated offline modes share the injected-backend futures for
  paced concurrency/prefill, scheduled request rate, and user-centric target users.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-ancillary-timing-policy-design.md` — **built +
  addendum**: Clock-driven Linear/Exponential/Poisson ramps, seeded warmup-aware
  Bernoulli fixed-delay policy, full-body send-complete HTTP 499 cancellation,
  and turn-zero round-robin with sticky session routing are implemented and
  wired into online issuers. Config v2 and runner phase DTOs expose applicable
  ramps, cancellation, and endpoint selection; graph phases consume arrival/
  prefill ramps and adaptive concurrency/prefill/request-rate controls through
  placement-wide worker updates.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-dag-branch-orchestrator-design.md` — **superseded by the
  `aiperf-graph` async-dataflow engine**: FORK/SPAWN fan-out = out-edges, join =
  `ChannelRequirement.count`, sticky-routing/drain-observer = deleted credit-protocol
  artifacts. Direct lowering, FORK/SPAWN materialization, whole-trace session/static-
  node bounds, and FAIL_FAST are built for runner `dag_jsonl`. Lineage doc.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-coverage-gap-ledger.md` — research synthesis of
  unspec'd bodies; addendum notes metrics, telemetry, and RNG gaps are now covered
  by dedicated specs/addenda.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-accuracy-accumulator-design.md` — **static and
  stateful runner paths built + addenda**:
  Rust owns inference/timing/metrics/reporting and supervised pinned Python
  workers own canonical datasets, environments, hidden tests, loops, and scoring.
  Static Lighteval and the stateful agentic pair are runner subprocess-tested.
  Harbor, AgentLab/BrowserGym, and MCPMark remain canonical Python providers;
  every model call returns through Rust's scheduled endpoint/transport path.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-metrics-accumulator-sweepline-design.md` — **built +
  addenda**: columnar/ragged engine, formulas/SLOs, full effective/active/ICL sweeps,
  duration-weighted stats, authoritative completion-usage reconciliation,
  windows/timeslices, worker merge, all-mode runtime wiring, deterministic
  per-model/per-endpoint native-v2 series, and the typed `Reporter`.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-metric-catalog-appendix.md` — **built + addendum**:
  103 inherited metric identities plus 16 sweep identities, exact metadata/formulas,
  dependency validation and fingerprint; GPU energy and network-adjusted rows inject
  when their optional producers are enabled.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-telemetry-accumulators-design.md` — **built + addenda**:
  `aiperf-gpu-telemetry`, `aiperf-server-metrics`, and `aiperf-network-latency`
  implement the shared side-channel accumulator seam, with `aiperf-server-metrics`
  owning its self-contained Prometheus/OpenMetrics parsing; `aiperf-runtime` owns their
  Clock-paced tasks, exact phase snapshots, finalize-order energy/network joins,
  GPU-energy accuracy analysis,
  native server report blocks, compatibility JSONL, fallback/auto-disable state
  machine, vLLM/SGLang atlas, histogram estimator, and TCP calibration.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-exporters-overhaul-design.md` — **built (see 2026-07-14
  addendum)**: the full native-Rust exporter plane (`aiperf_runtime::export`) is built and is
  the default sole emitter (`AIPERF_RUNTIME_NATIVE_EXPORT=0` restores legacy Python).
  Nine sinks behind one `Exporter` trait — aiperf-v1 (genai-perf-v1) JSON+CSV (incl. GPU `telemetry_data`), timeslice
  JSON+CSV, server-metrics JSON+CSV+parquet, accuracy CSV, console.txt (+warning/insight
  detectors), OTLP per-record metrics, MLflow, W&B — parity-verified byte-for-byte (or
  schema+data for parquet) vs the retired Python exporters via the `AIPERF_EXPORT_SUBDIR`
  same-report diff. Opt-in bounded-memory metrics: `AIPERF_METRICS_SKETCH=1` /
  `--sketch-metrics` (default off) swaps `MetricsStorageMode::Exact` for `Sketch`, streaming
  each Record-metric value into a per-`(phase, tag)` mergeable `cellular::sketch::TDigest`
  (exact count/sum/min/max + Welford std, approximate percentiles) so accumulator memory is
  O(1) in the record count; per-record artifacts + per-row-only outputs are dropped
  fail-closed (`rust_wire`, `validate_plan`), and the online path folds+drops each finalized
  record (`RunCapture::finish_fold_into`). Bounds the accumulator/coordinator finalize;
  online-path peak RSS still gated by per-worker record retention until drain (follow-up).
  Opt-in per-record sidecars: the `artifacts.records` format list takes `jsonl`, `csv`, and
  `parquet` (any subset, e.g. `records: [jsonl, csv, parquet]`). `parquet` writes a wide
  `profile_export.parquet` (one row per request, one nullable column per catalog record-metric,
  `aiperf.units` file metadata, `trace_*` columns when `artifacts.trace`); `csv` writes a flat
  `profile_export_records.csv` (metadata + a `{tag}_value`/`{tag}_unit` pair per metric +
  `error_code`/`error_type`/`error_message`, `trace_*` when trace on), ported from the legacy
  Python `RecordExportCsvResultsProcessor`. Runner-owned (not `Exporter`s over `NativeReport`):
  `rust/runtime/src/engine/records.rs::write_records_{parquet,csv}` drive the writers at the scheduled +
  graph callsites over the shared `aiperf_runtime::metrics_core::record_metric_columns`; parquet is gated
  on the `parquet` feature (a lite runner warns/skips), CSV is stdlib. Both are force-disabled on
  the DynoSim/sketch paths.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-endpoints-design.md` — **built + implementation/
  token-native addenda**: every tier-1 and tier-2 dialect plus the open PR-1113
  `vllm_generate` factory is implemented behind trait-backed prepared endpoints,
  including exact token-array accounting/non-text outputs, raw/template JMESPath + Jinja, and input-side ISL accounting.
  Multipart, Clock-paced polling/download, inline-media retrieval/deduplication, endpoint
  streaming paths, and lifecycle-wide post-send cancellation live in `aiperf-transport-http`;
  real-loopback tests cover the dialect families, wire lifecycles, and native modality metrics.
  Its endpoint-identity/registry/config-ownership claims are superseded by the runner-owned
  endpoint-registry spec; its formatting/parsing/replay behavior remains authoritative.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-rng-derive-system-design.md` — the hash-derived
  RNG substrate: `blake3(f"{root}:{id}")[:8]`→u64 order-independent seed derivation
  + canonical namespace constants + `HashIdRandomGenerator` (per-`(trace_id,
  hash_id)` reseed) + `RandomGenerator` and generic sampler contracts; ruling: NO
  cross-language byte parity — one deterministic PRNG (`Pcg64`) + `rand_distr`
  with faithful distribution/edge-case semantics; internal reproducibility +
  order-independence (lock-free per-thread, alloc-free reseed). Built as leaf crate
  `aiperf-rng`; a Rust-internal fixed-seed profile canary pins the stream. Dataset
  composition/samplers, recorded WEKA/Dynamo content synthesis, ancillary timing policies, and graph phase/arrival/
  node-cancellation/worker streams consume it; broader non-graph scheduler
  integration remains.
- `specs/2026-07-09-graph-ir-rust-port-design.md` — Graph-IR runtime plus direct
  authored `dag_jsonl`, `weka_trace`, and `dynamo_trace` lowering are built in
  `aiperf-graph`; addenda supersede standalone/offline-only and parse-plane
  non-goal framing with the current `LocalSet` + `drive_sim`/`drive_real` +
  HTTP-dispatch path, runner-only `graph` workload, and canonical `aiperf-rng`
  BLAKE3 recorded-content synthesis.
- `specs/2026-07-13-scheduled-graph-production-convergence.md` — **code-grounded
  audit**: the scheduled and graph online paths already share `TransportSink`,
  `PreparedHttpTurn`, `NativeMetricsObserver`, the `IntervalGenerator`/`SlotPool`
  primitives, and the phase orchestrator; graph arrival/admission are thin
  wrappers over the same primitives. Only failure behavior genuinely differs
  (graph fail-fast/abort-run vs. scheduled resilient). Corrects the
  graph-is-metrics-lite impression; flags incidental cleanups; no refactor.
- `specs/2026-07-14-python-rust-timing-parity-proof.md` — **built + proven**:
  A/B every legacy timing mode under `AIPERF_RUNTIME_ENGINE=python` vs `rust`
  against a deterministic mock — worst response-timing divergence 1.06% (all
  within 5%), send-schedule adherence tighter than Python. Fixes: token-counting
  alignment (`--use-server-token-count`), fixed-schedule anchor→issuance-start,
  warm-start prewarm+lead barrier. Non-bugs: RNG-stream variance, Python
  saturation jitter.
- `specs/2026-07-13-p1-generic-execution-substrate-names.md` — **P1 naming pass**
  (built: renames + fold; `inference_dimensions` signature kept by design — see
  the 2026-07-14 addenda): give the already-shared execution substrate one generic
  vocabulary. The DTO/placement/method renames and the dispatch-method fold landed
  (collect surface → two primitives).
  `PreparedHttpTurn`/`MeasuredTurn*`/`HttpTurnDispatchResult` →
  `PreparedTurn`/`Measured*`/`DispatchResult`; placement seams →
  `RequestExecutor` (per-request) / `TracePlacement` (per-trace). Pure rename +
  de-dup, no behavior change; does not merge the seams (deferred).
- `specs/2026-07-13-greenfield-execution-vocabulary.md` — **north-star vocabulary**
  (design, converged via naming review): the unconstrained-ideal names for the v2
  unified substrate. Four work levels `Replay` → `Trace` (definition) → `Session`
  (in-flight instance) → `Request`; seams `BenchmarkRun`/`Phase`/`Workload`/`Pacer`/
  `SlotPool`/`StopCondition`/`WorkerPool`/`Dispatcher`/`Observer`/`OnFailure`/`Clock`
  (`MonotonicClock`/`VirtualClock`). Deletes the executor tier and `Admission`
  outright. Destination the P1 renames walk toward; not an incremental plan.
- `specs/2026-07-13-scheduled-graph-convergence-implementation.md` — **built**:
  implements the convergence trio. The audit's one deferred decision (failure
  behavior) ships as the greenfield `OnFailure { Continue, Abort }` enum shared by
  scheduled and graph, wired through an optional `cfg.failure_policy` (absent →
  each path's historical default, no regression); graph `Continue` uses the
  dormant `Resilient`/`Continue` library policies, scheduled `Abort` latches a
  `Failed`-terminal `bail!`. Keeps `DurationGraphStop`/`ScheduledGraphArrival` as
  documented unwired seams; documents why scheduled streaming dispatch stays off.
  Carries the P1 rename pass (DTO/placement/method renames, landed after the
  concurrent bodyplan work committed `http.rs`); the P1 method-fold,
  `inference_dimensions` signature change, and discarded-observer cleanup stay deferred.
- `specs/2026-07-14-unified-execution-substrate-design.md` — **north-star;
  Stage 1 built**: one `Dispatcher`, one `WorkerPool`, any workload over any
  transport. **Stage 1 shipped**: an object-safe `Dispatcher` trait
  (`dispatch_collect(PreparedTurn)`) implemented once per transport
  (`TransportSink`/`GrpcTransportSink`); the graph sink holds `Rc<dyn Dispatcher>`;
  the graph endpoint runtime factory builds an HTTP or gRPC dispatcher from
  `cfg.transport.type`; and the whole `RunnerPairFactory` layer — `pairs` map,
  `register_pair`, the pair impls, **and** the `validate_descriptor_compatibility`
  predicate / `supported_pairs` inventory — is **deleted**. Transports and
  workloads are two independent registries with **no compatibility gate**; every
  workload runs over every transport, `prepare`/`validate_run` moved onto the
  workload factory. Deliverable proven: `transport.type: grpc` + a `dag_jsonl`
  graph dataset dispatches graph nodes over Tonic (`rust/cli/tests/test_graph_grpc.rs`).
  Supersedes the `RunnerPairFactory` mechanism of the runner-only execution-surface
  spec (its 2026-07-14 addendum). Stage 2 (`WorkerPool`/`Session` merge) is design-only.
- `specs/2026-07-13-segment-unification-design.md` — **segment unification**
  (design): collapse `Turn`'s five body fields (content/messages/raw_payload/
  raw_messages/raw_token_ids) into segment `Handle`s in the one `SegmentPool`;
  lowering = the single compiler; dispatch materializes one `Full<Bytes>` by
  concat-not-reserialize with the segment **domain as discriminant** (`raw` = 12 ns
  clone, `message` = splice). Live continuation = runtime segments (O(depth²) but
  cheap). Endpoint formatter runs at **lowering, not dispatch** (not-slow
  requirement). Honors the single-`Full`-buffer + `SendCompletion` constraint (no
  scatter-gather). Grounded in segment.rs/request.rs/model.rs/connection.rs + microbench.
- `specs/2026-07-13-endpoint-body-construction-design.md` — **endpoint formatter
  split** (design): `format_payload → BodyPlan` (named fields; value = literal or
  segment `Handle`). JSON endpoints (`transport::http`) **splice** segment bytes into
  one `Full<Bytes>` (generalizes `build_message_body_from_wires`+`Overrides`; zero
  content re-serialize); protobuf endpoints (`transport::grpc`) pack token/tensor
  segments into `raw_input_contents` — **no per-request `Value`/per-element walk**
  (Python PR #664 = what-not-to-port). Formatter runs at lowering; endpoints declare
  shape; splicing is one shared impl. Dispatch-side companion to segment-unification.
- `specs/2026-07-13-websocket-transport-design.md` — **WebSocket inference
  transport** (design, not built): Clock-injected `transport_ws` modeled on
  **Codex's** WS turn stream (WS-primary + **HTTPS/SSE fallback**); OpenAI
  **Realtime** a distinct dialect — never conflated with the generic Responses API.
  Third `BodyPlan` materializer (`→ WS frames`; concat-not-reserialize, no
  per-request `Value`), streaming/session dispatch (gRPC-bidi precedent), per-frame
  `RequestObserver` measurement, SSE fallback reuses `transport::http`.
  **upstream** `tokio-tungstenite` (`MaybeTlsStream`, single-task unsplit drive);
  one-shot WS→SSE fallback latch, text-only frames; completeness gated on the
  terminal event not the socket FIN; benign-close taxonomy. Single-`Full`/
  `SendCompletion` stays HTTP-local.
- `specs/2026-07-09-dynamo-aiperf-{shared-core,request-rate-tokenizer}-design.md`
  — historical precursors (built on dynamo's `lib/mocker`; superseded by the
  standalone workspace).
- `specs/2026-07-12-track-a-*.md` + `specs/2026-07-12-{scheduled-worker-local-accumulation,http-connector-seam-uds-duplex,lean-per-request-hotpath,single-observer-compat-projection,cellular-ready-seams-and-roadmap}.md`
  — **PR1 + PR2 (A1) built; A3/A4/A2 planning.** The Track-A measurement-path
  refactor design set: implementation plan (PR1 `RunCapture` uuid-keyed join
  **(built)** → A1 worker-local accumulation **(built, runner HTTP + gRPC via an
  additive `execute_turn_measured`/`drain_records` seam; `BufferedObserver` kept
  for agentic/evaluation)** → A3 connector / A4 lean → A2 compat projection),
  regression harnesses, the four component specs, and the cellular-ready seams +
  roadmap (single-issuer today, cross-node autonomous cells deferred). Start with
  `specs/2026-07-12-track-a-implementation.md`.
- `specs/2026-07-15-cellular-horizontal-scale-k6-parity-design.md`
  — **path to k6-class horizontal scale without losing measurement fidelity.**
  Verified against `grafana/k6` source that AIPerf already owns k6's hard part
  (master-less static execution partition; k6 `execution_segment.go` == AIPerf
  `owned_positions`/`CellularAutonomousIssuer`). The gap is the results plane:
  AIPerf is a star topology with byte-exact retain merge, k6 streams bounded
  aggregates to a scalable sink. Proposes a **scale-adaptive fidelity ladder**
  (T0 exact default → T1 bounded sketch → T2 tree-merge → T3 external-sink) so
  compromises (approx percentiles, no per-record artifacts, looser start) are
  gated behind scale; counts/sums/rates stay exact at every tier. Six ordered
  steps; recommended first cut = Steps 1+2 (sketch `StorePartition` ship +
  streaming per-worker fold-and-drop) = tier T1, ~80% of k6 scale for ~20% of
  the work, no velo change, T0 byte-exact preserved as default.
- `specs/2026-07-15-velo-cell-transport-design.md` + `specs/2026-07-15-ultimate-cellular-velo-runtime-design.md`
  — **the cellular cross-host + north-star pair.** The velo transport swap is
  **built** (connect-by-endpoint on the `feat/connect-by-endpoint` velo fork:
  `Velo::connect(Endpoint)`/`_hello`; four `aiperf.cell.*` rmp handlers;
  synchronized START via a velo `EventHandle` + an AIPerf-side count barrier;
  Stages B–G HTTP+zstd artifact/dataset shipping; k8s operator/JobSet
  zero-discovery emptyDir launch; multi-turn exact-fold + graph cellular). The
  **ultimate** spec is the Phase-3+ north-star (designed, not built): dataset
  fan-out over a **producer-owned SPMC add-only broadcast anchor velo must add**
  (velo today has only SPSC/MPSC consumer-owned anchors, no replay, no fan-out;
  rendezvous RDMA is Phase-2-unbuilt), a **monotonic phaser** control plane
  (synchronized START generalized to every phase transition, cyclic), a
  per-request dispatch state machine with a counted `DistributionMiss`, and
  bounded-memory record collection (ship the merged t-digest sketch as a
  `StorePartition`). It supersedes the two prior cellular specs going forward.

## Build / test / run

Use `cargo build --release`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, and
`cargo fmt` for Rust development. Build the feature-bearing `aiperf` binary with
`cargo build -p aiperf-cli --features dynosim`. Package the **single `aiperf`
wheel** (maturin backend, root `pyproject.toml`) with `make wheel`:
`make bundle-cli` builds the full-fat unified `aiperf` binary (`lto=fat`, crate
default `--features full`); `maturin build` emits one platform-specific wheel
carrying the `pyext` `aiperf._native` module and the `src/aiperf` frontend; and
`tools/wheel_repack.py` then repacks the binary directly into the wheel's scripts
directory as `aiperf-<ver>.data/scripts/aiperf` — no separate
`aiperf`/`aiperf_rust` wheel. The installed `aiperf` command IS the native
binary. End users run `aiperf profile --config benchmark.yaml`; the pure-Python
frontend is reachable as `aiperf-python` and `python -m aiperf`.
`cargo run -p aiperf-runtime` and native `--offline`/mode flags do not exist.
